sources.name: digiKam advanced search and metadata model
sources.reuse: Use DAM-style facets: tags, labels, ratings, date, location and metadata search.

sources.name: Alcedo Studio
sources.reuse: Borrow lightweight RAW/DAM workspace ideas: AI tags, natural-language search, keeper curation.

sources.name: Awesome Stock Resources
sources.reuse: Use license-based source categories for external photo/video resources.

sources.name: Awesome Open Source Photography
sources.reuse: Use photography workflow categories: RAW developers, organizers, EXIF editors, tethering, color correction, video tools.

sources.name: Shot Type Classifier
sources.reuse: Use the six cinematic shot sizes as normalized shot-size values.

sources.name: Movie Shot Classification Dataset
sources.reuse: Use camera movement classes for video and short-form reference notes.

sources.name: Image Composition Assessment Dataset CADB
sources.reuse: Use scene category, composition class, composition element and quality score ideas for reference scoring.

sources.name: G'MIC Film LUTs Collection
sources.reuse: Use film-emulation LUT library categories and .cube asset fields.

sources.name: Raw Alchemy
sources.reuse: Use explicit color-space pipeline fields before applying creative LUTs to photos.

sources.name: apply-cube-lut
sources.reuse: Use .cube parsing/application concepts for future preview and LUT matching.

sources.name: SDXL Style Reference
sources.reuse: Use public-domain photographic style prompt structure for AI previsualization.

adoptionPlan: Keep current Chinese shooting-specific fields, but add open-standard fields for interoperability.
Normalize shotSize and cameraMovement values to open filmmaking taxonomies.
Track licenseClass for every external source, especially stock and platform references.
Prepare future EXIF/IPTC/XMP read-write so final works can carry tags and captions outside the app.
Treat LUT entries as color pipelines, not just style names.

scoring.authority: 0-25: standard body, paper, maintained project, or informal repo
scoring.dataSufficiency: 0-25: dataset size, taxonomy completeness, field coverage
scoring.integrationFit: 0-15: can be cleanly mapped into PhotoAtelier without heavy dependency

adoptionLevels.adopt: Use directly as schema/taxonomy field source.
adoptionLevels.adapt: Use concepts and normalized labels, but keep local heuristics and manual review.
adoptionLevels.reference: Keep as inspiration only; do not import assets or rely on it for production decisions.
adoptionLevels.reject: Do not use until license/data/maintenance concerns are resolved.

sources.name: IPTC Photo Metadata Standard 2025.1
sources.professionalCertification: Formal IPTC standard governed by the IPTC Photo Metadata Working Group and IPTC Standards Committee.
sources.dataSufficiency: High. Covers administrative, descriptive and rights-related photo metadata; latest version adds AI prompt metadata.
sources.communityFeedback: High industry adoption. IPTC states its fields are widely supported by imaging software and integrate with DAM systems.
sources.licenseAssessment: Documentation is public; use as schema guidance, not asset content.
risks: Does not define camera technical metadata; use EXIF/XMP for capture/edit history.
evidence: Specification says IPTC Photo Metadata properties are widely supported by imaging software.
2025.1 adds AI Prompt Information, AI Prompt Writer Name, AI System Used and AI System Version Used.
User Guide is for photographers, photo editors and metadata managers.

howToCallInProject.current: Map title, description, creator, copyright, keywords, sourceUrl, rightsUsageTerms and aiPromptInfo fields.
howToCallInProject.next: When exporting final images, write IPTC/XMP sidecar or embedded metadata via ExifTool.

sources.name: digiKam DAM model
sources.professionalCertification: No standards-body certification, but mature KDE-family open-source DAM application.
sources.dataSufficiency: High for workflow fields: albums, tags, ratings, labels, dates, locations and EXIF/IPTC/XMP metadata search.
sources.communityFeedback: High product maturity signal: long-running open-source project, cross-platform, documented features.
sources.licenseAssessment: Use ideas/schema; do not embed code.
risks: digiKam is an application model, not a formal schema standard.
evidence: digiKam describes itself as an advanced open-source digital photo management application.
It supports organizing with tags, ratings and labels.
Its advanced search covers tags, labels, ratings, date, location and EXIF/IPTC/XMP metadata.

howToCallInProject.current: Use as reference for filters and database facets: tag, rating, label, date, location, metadata.
howToCallInProject.next: Add rating/label filters to PhotoAtelier reference page and final-work import flow.

sources.name: Alcedo Studio
sources.professionalCertification: No formal certification. Active open-source project, not a standard.
sources.dataSufficiency: Medium-high for product design patterns: RAW editor, DAM, AI tags, natural language search, ratings, EXIF facets.
sources.communityFeedback: Moderate. GitHub page showed 151 stars, 3 forks, 1 issue and 1,025 commits at audit time.
sources.licenseAssessment: GPL-3.0. Do not copy code into this project unless compatible; use concepts only.
risks: Project says it is not an alternative to existing commercial/open-source projects.
Heavy C++/GPU app; too large to integrate directly.
evidence: README describes RAW editor and DAM with AI layer.
Features include semantic labels, natural-language search and local vector index.
Library browser includes facets, ratings, import/export and metadata handling.

howToCallInProject.current: Borrow UX/data concepts: AI labels, semantic search, keeper score, local-first privacy.
howToCallInProject.next: Implement our own lightweight image embedding/tag cache; do not vendor Alcedo code.

sources.name: Shot Type Classifier
sources.professionalCertification: No formal certification. Informal applied ML project.
sources.dataSufficiency: Medium. Six cinematic shot-size classes are useful; model/data should not be treated as production-grade.
sources.communityFeedback: Moderate. GitHub page showed 209 stars and 40 forks at audit time.
sources.licenseAssessment: CC BY-NC 4.0. Non-commercial license means do not copy model/data into commercial workflows.
risks: Useful taxonomy, not enough as a reliable classifier for this app.
evidence: README lists six shot types.
Usage predicts shot types into CSV.
Repository license is Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0.

howToCallInProject.current: Use the six labels only as normalized values.
howToCallInProject.next: If automatic shot classification is needed, train/choose a commercially safe model separately.

sources.name: Movie Shot Classification Dataset
sources.professionalCertification: Academic paper citation: Iberian Conference on Pattern Recognition and Image Analysis, Springer, 2022.
sources.dataSufficiency: Medium-high. 1,803 classified film-shot instances across 10 camera movement classes.
sources.communityFeedback: Low GitHub popularity but academically cited. GitHub page showed 11 stars and 1 fork at audit time.
sources.licenseAssessment: MIT license. Safe for taxonomy/data reference subject to citation.
risks: Film-shot data may not transfer perfectly to portrait short-video workflows.
evidence: Dataset lists 10 camera movement classes and counts totaling 1,803.
README provides a paper citation.
License shown as MIT.

howToCallInProject.current: Use its camera movement classes for video reference metadata.
howToCallInProject.next: Add manual cameraMovement selector in short-video planning UI.

sources.name: Image Composition Assessment Dataset CADB
sources.dataSufficiency: High. 9,497 images; each image rated by 5 fine-art-specialized raters; scene categories, composition classes and composition elements released.
sources.communityFeedback: Moderate. GitHub page showed 173 stars, 15 forks and 3 issues at audit time.
sources.licenseAssessment: MIT license for repository. Dataset use should still follow repo download terms.
risks: Composition score is aesthetic research, not direct client preference.
Images may not match Chinese social-platform portrait trends.
evidence: README calls it the first image composition assessment dataset.
Dataset has 9,497 images rated by 5 fine-art-specialized raters.
2022 update released scene categories, composition classes and composition elements.

howToCallInProject.current: Use composition classes/elements and compositionScore as reference fields.
howToCallInProject.next: Add optional composition scoring for imported final works.

sources.name: G'MIC Film LUTs Collection
sources.dataSufficiency: Medium. Contains LUT folder, thumbnails and JSON index, useful for structure.
sources.communityFeedback: Moderate. GitHub page showed 201 stars and 27 forks at audit time.
sources.licenseAssessment: MIT repository, but README disclaimer says LUTs may be subject to third-party copyright/trademarks; do not import LUT files directly.
risks: Maintainer disclaims responsibility for LUT use.
evidence: README says LUTs are for creative and educational purposes.
README warns LUTs may be subject to copyrights and trademarks.
Repository includes film_luts.json and LUT assets.

howToCallInProject.current: Use only the index shape: lutName, thumbnail, compatibleSoftware, rightsReviewRequired.
howToCallInProject.next: Create our own LUT metadata entries; only link external LUTs, never bundle until each license is verified.

sources.name: Raw Alchemy
sources.professionalCertification: No formal certification, but it is a focused color-science tool with documented GUI/CLI workflow.
sources.dataSufficiency: High for color-pipeline concepts: RAW decoding, log conversion, LUT expected input space, lens profiles.
sources.communityFeedback: Good. GitHub page showed 439 stars, AGPL-3.0 license and 97 commits at audit time.
sources.licenseAssessment: AGPL-3.0. Do not copy code into closed/local project without accepting copyleft obligations; use CLI externally or reimplement concepts.
evidence: README explains RAW photos directly applying video LUTs can fail due to color-space mismatch.
CLI syntax supports input RAW path and output TIFF path.
Topics include color-science, LUT, color-grading, raw-processing and log-profile.

howToCallInProject.current: Adopt color pipeline fields: inputColorSpace, logProfile, lutExpectedInput, outputSpace.
howToCallInProject.next: Optional external CLI integration only; keep project data-layer independent.

sources.name: Awesome Stock Resources
sources.dataSufficiency: Medium for discovering source sites; low for verified licensing because each target site has separate terms.
sources.communityFeedback: Requires periodic review; not authoritative enough for rights decisions by itself.
sources.licenseAssessment: Use as discovery list only; verify each platform license separately.
evidence: Repository is a collection of links for free stock photography, video and illustration websites.

howToCallInProject.current: Use to expand external platform list.
howToCallInProject.next: For each platform, add separate license audit before surfacing as commercial-safe.

sources.name: SDXL Style Reference
sources.dataSufficiency: Low-medium. Useful prompt phrasing examples, not photography taxonomy or validated data.
sources.communityFeedback: Useful but model-specific; not enough for production taxonomy.
sources.licenseAssessment: Only use as prompt pattern inspiration; do not treat styles as rights-cleared.
risks: Optimized for a specific SDXL mix
May encode style names with rights/personality concerns.
evidence: Repository describes a list of Stable Diffusion style prompts optimized for RobMix Zenith.

howToCallInProject.current: Do not directly import; keep AI previsualization prompts local and generic.
howToCallInProject.next: Build our own prompt library from approved styles and user outcomes.

items.sourceFile: 摄影姿势库/汉服/室内汉服/pose_侧坐案前.md
items.summary: 侧坐案前 动作要点 1. 坐姿 ：侧身坐于案几旁，上身微转，不要正对镜头 2. 手部 ：单手轻拈花枝/珍珠，另一手自然置于膝上 3. 眼神 ：视线投向斜上方或看手中物，不看镜头 4. 身体 ：肩、胯形成微小三才转折，身体有曲线感 关键细节 坐姿忌僵硬，腰背挺直但肩部放松 手部动作是重点——兰花指、轻捻珍珠都很有古韵 可在身前地面散落珍珠/花瓣增加氛围 利用倒
